carousels.title: When your AI vendor gets it wrong, you’re still responsible
carousels.cover_text: AI vendor screw-up? YOU eat the cost.
carousels.caption:
Your AI vendor getting it wrong is NOT a free pass. The OCC, GSEs, and Treasury all agree: you're still on the hook for decisions influenced by AI, especially with Fannie's new guidance coming. This isn't just about compliance; it's about protecting your pipeline and P&L. If you're using AI in any part of your process – from lead generation to loan servicing – you need to understand the implications of vendor risk. It's time to scrutinize contracts and ensure your internal controls are robust. Don't let an AI error become your company's liability. Plan now for what happens when vendor AI makes a bad call. It's not a matter of if, but when. Are your contracts ready?

Source : https://tinyurl.com/25sv2vuc
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #mortgagecompliance #aiforbusiness #mortgageservicing
carousels.hook: AI vendor error? The buck stops with YOU.
carousels.what_happened: Mortgage servicers remain responsible for account decisions influenced by vendor AI. This is true under OCC model risk guidance, GSE requirements, and Treasury AI controls.

breakdown.heading: Fannie's New Rule
breakdown.body: Fannie Mae's LL-2026-04 takes effect August 6, 2026. This mandate makes your AI practices a key part of your relationship with them.

breakdown.heading: What Underwriting Sees
breakdown.body: When a file hits underwriting, any AI-driven decision will be scrutinized. We don't care who coded it; we care about the decision's validity and compliance.

breakdown.heading: Inventory Your AI
breakdown.body: You need an inventory of all AI tools used, especially vendor-supplied ones. Understanding their function and potential impact is critical for risk assessment.

breakdown.heading: Stronger Contracts Needed
breakdown.body: Review your vendor contracts. Ensure they include robust terms on indemnification and data accuracy when AI is part of their service.

carousels.my_take_heading: My Take: It's Not 'Their' AI Problem
carousels.my_take: Many think vendor AI means vendor liability. Wrong. You're the one holding the bag. Plan for AI failure like you plan for any other operational risk.
carousels.action_lo: Understand how AI is used in your lead gen or processing. Can you articulate its output if questioned by underwriting?
carousels.action_realtor: Be aware if your lender partners are using AI. Ask them about their processes for accuracy and compliance.
carousels.cta_question: What's your plan for when a vendor's AI inevitably makes a mistake?

carousels.title: Kim Smith on SmartFi’s strategy to grow the reverse mortgage pie
carousels.cover_text: Forward LOs: untapped reverse mortgage gold.
carousels.caption:
The reverse mortgage market is poised for significant growth, not by focusing solely on existing reverse specialists, but by empowering forward-centric loan officers. Think about your existing database: how many clients over 62 are sitting on substantial home equity? This strategy isn't just about diversification; it's about providing a complete solution set for your clients throughout their homeownership journey. When a file comes to underwriting, a reverse mortgage looks different, but the core principles of asset and income verification remain. The key is understanding how to present it as a strategic financial tool, not a last resort. Don't leave money on the table – educate your team and unlock this overlooked segment of the market. Who in your pipeline could benefit from this conversation?

Source : https://tinyurl.com/2dzo3kgd
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #reversemortgage #loanofficer #mortgagebroker
carousels.hook: The biggest reverse mortgage growth is NOT where you think.
carousels.what_happened: SmartFi's strategy aims to grow the reverse mortgage market by equipping traditional, forward-centric loan officers. This involves providing them with the tools and education to offer reverse mortgages to their clients.

breakdown.heading: Access Existing Relationships
breakdown.body: Forward LOs already have trusted relationships with clients. This makes them ideal for introducing complex products like reverse mortgages.

breakdown.heading: Underwriter View: Asset-Rich Clients
breakdown.body: Underwriting sees many clients with significant home equity but limited liquidity. Reverse mortgages can bridge that gap, turning illiquid equity into usable funds.

breakdown.heading: Not a Niche Product Anymore
breakdown.body: Treating reverse mortgages as a niche limits growth. Integrating them into a full product suite diversifies your offerings and client solutions.

breakdown.heading: Education is Key
breakdown.body: The biggest hurdle is often a lack of LO education. Training on how reverse products actually function and serve client needs is crucial.

carousels.my_take_heading: My Take: Stop Ignoring Your Best Prospect List
carousels.my_take: Your existing book of business is gold. Many homeowners over 62 could benefit from a reverse mortgage, and you're already their trusted advisor. The opportunity is staring us in the face.
carousels.action_lo: Identify clients aged 62+ in your database. Proactively educate yourself and them on how reverse mortgages can be a powerful financial tool.
carousels.action_realtor: Partner with LOs who understand reverse mortgages. This helps your senior clients make smart moves, whether buying, selling, or staying put.
carousels.cta_question: How many clients in your existing database are missing out on reverse mortgage solutions?

carousels.title: Home Equity Loans Capture Record Share As Homeowners Stay Put
carousels.caption:
Home equity loans and HELOCs are no longer just niche products; they're becoming the primary way homeowners access cash without giving up their low first mortgage rates. With record-low recapture rates on refinances, this shift isn't surprising. From an underwriting perspective, these loans present different risks and opportunities, focusing heavily on current LTV and DTI, not just the original purchase. This trend is a massive signal: homeowners are staying put, and they need strategic ways to leverage their equity. Are you equipped to serve this growing segment? If not, you're leaving a significant portion of the market to competitors. This isn't a temporary fad; it's a structural change in how people use their homes as financial assets. Adapt or get left behind.

Source : https://tinyurl.com/23sdqucr
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #homeequity #heloc #mortgageindustry
carousels.hook: Homeowners are getting cash without refinancing. Are you ready?
carousels.what_happened_heading: The News: Record Home Equity Share
carousels.what_happened: Homeowners are increasingly using HELOCs and second mortgages to access cash without refinancing their low first-mortgage rates. This pushed home equity lending to a record share of mortgage transactions in 2025.

breakdown.heading: Growth is Significant
breakdown.body: Home equity loan volume increased 15% between 2021 and 2025. This growth signals a major shift in how homeowners access capital.

breakdown.heading: Underwriter Lens: LTV vs. DTI
breakdown.body: When a file hits underwriting, these loans emphasize current LTV (loan-to-value) and DTI (debt-to-income). The borrower’s original purchase price is less relevant.

breakdown.heading: Retention Opportunity
breakdown.body: With refinance recapture rates around 20-30%, home equity products are crucial. They keep clients engaged with you even when rates are high.

breakdown.heading: It's Not Just a Refi Alternative
breakdown.body: This isn't a temporary workaround. Home equity products are becoming a primary, strategic financial tool for long-term homeowners.

carousels.my_take_heading: My Take: Home Equity IS the New Refinance
carousels.my_take: Stop treating home equity products as secondary. For many, they're the only viable option to tap wealth without rate shock. This is where your clients are moving.
carousels.action_lo: Actively market home equity products. Re-engage past clients with low rates to show them how they can still access their equity.
carousels.action_realtor: Educate clients on how HELOCs or second mortgages can finance improvements. This makes homes more attractive, or helps buyers with down payment strategies.
carousels.cta_question: Are you leaving money on the table by underemphasizing home equity products?
